New Label

A label is a banner on the chart, not a task. It has no progress, no status and no dependencies, and nothing counts it — not the task totals, the actions list, the dashboard or the critical path. Use it for a shift window, a period of overall command, or a plain note.

Categories

People directory

People here can be set as a task's responsible person, added to teams and placed on the org chart. Contact numbers and e-mail addresses entered here follow the person everywhere, including the org chart and its exports.

What you get — one workbook, eight sheets

Schedule — the Gantt: groups, tasks, milestones, colour-coded bars, frozen panes, collapsible groupsmain
Actions — every action with owner, team, status, progress and due datefilterable
Teams — roster, person in charge, roles and each team's workload
Team Timeline — one lane per team with its work beneath
Against the Clock — every team on ONE line, each activity a labelled bar, with the shift, command and tool box talk bands abovenew
Shift Plan — when each team is really on site (an hour away splits the bar), what each shift covers and who holds commandnew
Task Data — flat table for pivots
Cover — KPIs, contents, legend and summariesindex
Every sheet carries a navigation bar, and task names, team names and the contents page are hyperlinked so reviewers can click straight through.

The whole programme is fitted to the width — no toolbars, no scrollbars, nothing but the chart.

Progress bar colours

A bar shows the finished share in the completed colour; the rest takes the colour of its status. These colours are used on the chart, in the image export, in the slides and in Excel.
CompletedThe finished portion of any bar
In progressThe outstanding portion of work under way
Not startedNothing done yet
BlockedHeld up — defaults to the same red
Group summary barThe roll-up bar above each group

Project actions

Shifts & overall command

A closure is more than a task list — it runs in shifts, it is briefed at tool box talks, and at any moment one named person holds overall command. Tool box talks are picked up from the programme automatically (any task with “tool box” or “briefing” in its name). Shifts and command periods are set here, and both are written into the Against the Clock and Shift Plan sheets of the Excel pack.

Shifts

Overall command

Send a view-only copy

This packs the whole application and the current plan into one HTML file inside a zip. The recipient unzips it, double-clicks the file and sees everything — no install, no network, and nothing to load. Every editing control is switched off in their copy.

Publish to GitHub

Not connected

This writes the programme straight into your repository as a single commit. Everyone who has the web link picks it up automatically — the page they have open checks for a new version and offers them a Reload.

Access token

The token is kept in this browser on this computer and nowhere else. It is never written into the programme file, never committed, and never travels in a share link — so nobody opening the published page can publish with it.

About this build

Gantt Studio

Revision J23 Aug 2026

One self-contained HTML file. No server, no install, no network — the whole application, its data and every export are built inside this page. It can even copy itself: Share packs a read-only version of the whole programme into a zip you can send.

RevisionJ
Revision date26 August 2026
Developed byD&IS Project Technical Manager
E-mail—
Telephone—
StorageBrowser local storage
New in Revision V
· Move, resize, rotate and duplicate on a map — every drawn thing now has eight handles and a rotation grip, and a pin, a person or a text label finally has a box you can grab instead of a zero-sized point. Hold Shift while resizing to keep the proportions, or while rotating to snap to 15°. Ctrl+D copies the selection clear of the original, names the copy, and — if you copied a motion path along with what rides it — makes the copy ride the copy.
· Named motion paths — a path shows no label on the map, so before now it had no identity at all. Every element carries a name, the new On this map list shows all of them, and the Motion menu says which path drives what.
· Export a map — as an animated GIF that plays on its own inside PowerPoint, Word and Excel; as a WebM video; as a single self-contained HTML file where the animation is real vector motion; or as a high-resolution PNG or SVG still. The dialog estimates the size before you commit.
· Strike out instead of deleting — when work is dropped but not yet settled, strike it out. It stays on the chart, ruled through, so the decision is visible — but nothing counts it, totals it, schedules it or exports it. Put it back whenever you like.
· Mark complete — one button sets the task to 100%, stamps the date it was finished, and ticks every sub-task. The completion date is saved, shown on the row and carried into the Excel pack.
· Work locations — a managed register of the places work happens, which can nest (BP10 › CER › Rack row 2). Tag a task to a place, filter on it — a parent takes everything beneath it — and read the new Locations tab, where each place gets a lane on its own timeline and double-booked rooms are called out.
· Reorder team lanes — move a team up or down from its card, the list or the timeline, and the team timeline follows.
· Situation update for WhatsApp — a six-hourly management update built from the programme: RAG status, progress against plan, what is running, what is at risk, what is next, plus your own lines. Copy the text, save a picture card sized for a phone, open WhatsApp with the message already written, or post it straight through the Cloud API. The access token is held in the tab only and is never written into the project file.
· A window note that follows what you are looking at — the status bar used to report the whole programme whatever was on screen. It now reports the filtered set, or the task you have selected, with the dates, the count and the duration, so there is nothing left to work out by eye.

Revision U
· Maps — a new tab. Put a floor plan, a track schematic or any picture behind a canvas and draw over it: areas, free shapes, arrows, pins, text and people. Tie any of them to a task, a team or a person and it takes that colour, name and dates. Draw a motion path and send an element along it, then press Show for a full-screen walk-through. Maps can be searched, renamed, duplicated and deleted, and they travel inside the programme file.
· Labels on the chart — the Label button adds a banner to any group: a shift window, a period of overall command, or a plain note. A label is never a task — no progress, no status, no dependencies, and nothing counts it. It draws as a band on the Gantt and exports as one to Excel. Shifts & overall command now reads and writes these labels, so there is one place to enter a shift.
· Teams search — one box over the Teams page that matches a team by its name, its person in charge or any member, and a person by name or role, across all three views.

Revision T
· Shifts & overall command — a closure runs in shifts, is briefed at tool box talks and has one named person holding command at any moment. Set the shift windows and the command periods under Project actions → Shifts & overall command (or press Build from tool box talks and let the programme write them for you). They are saved with the plan.
· Two new Excel sheets — Against the Clock puts every team on one line with each activity as a labelled bar, and Shift Plan shows when each team is really on site, splitting the bar wherever a team is away for more than an hour. Both carry the shift bands, the tool box talks and the command bands across the top, and both follow the filters and the column scale you chose — so a single closure day at 30-minute columns reads exactly like the table-top exercise chart.

Revision S
· Excel timeline — one column for one date — the day scale now walks the dates one at a time, every date in order, with the month and year on the band above and the first of each month marked in the box. Auto reaches for week and month columns only past a year of work, so a Day-Zero build-up or a month of works no longer collapses into columns that jump seven days at a time. The 30-minute, hourly and 2-hourly closure scales from Revision R are unchanged.

Revision R
· Excel timeline down to 30 minutes — the Excel export can now cut the Gantt into 30-minute, hourly or two-hourly columns instead of whole days. Every box carries its clock time, the full date sits on the band above and is repeated in the box at each midnight, and a heavier line marks where one day ends and the next begins — so a single night's closure reads as a real shift chart. A one- or two-day filter picks 30 minutes automatically, and a span too long for the chosen step is widened rather than producing thousands of columns.

Revision Q
· Org chart — add what you like — Add to chart now offers a person from the directory, a whole team as its own box, or a blank role. A team box carries the team's name, colour, size and lead straight from the Teams page, and can bring its members in as reports in one click. The sidebar has a People / Teams switch, and Edit box converts any box between the three.

Revision P
· Schedule order — the toolbar Sort button (or a click on any column heading) puts the task / group list into name order, timeline order, duration or progress order; Manual order gives your hand-made order back and re-enables row dragging. Excel, PowerPoint and image exports follow whatever order is on screen.
· Compact org chart — Process now stacks a team of plain reports into a few short columns hanging off a spine instead of one very wide row, so the whole structure fits on the screen. The switch beside Process goes back to the classic one-row layout.
· Actions filter — the status row takes as many choices as you like; the list shows everything that matches any one of them.

Edit box

Changing Reports to does the same thing as dragging a handle from one box onto another. A box with no manager sits at the top of the chart.
